subject: DPA negotiation: retention lifecycle boundaries & onshore backup carveout
messages:
From: Olivia Martin <olivia.martin@aurum.ai>
To: rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@aurum.ai
Date: 2029-11-01T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: DPA redlines: retention windows & residency carveouts

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick product walkthrough last week. Our legal team has started a pass on the DPA and have a handful of retention/residency asks we need to resolve before procurement can move forward:

- Primary retention: we need a guaranteed 30-day minimum for user content (customer-managed dataset).
- Backups: can you confirm backup snapshots are retained for a maximum of 90 days and that restoration requires explicit authorization?
- Onshore backup option: for certain EU patient datasets we need an onshore (EU-located) backup copy and the ability to force-terminate cross-border replication on demand.
- Proof of deletion: our legal team requires a deletion manifest and a signed certificate of erasure within 10 business days of the request.
- Audit logs: we need audit logs for 12 months by default, but ability to restrict logs to 90 days for a given jurisdiction upon request.

I've attached our initial annotated redline (DPA_redlines_aurum_v2.docx). Can you loop in your security/ops folks to confirm feasibility and provide an ops-level erasure playbook? Also please propose language/value for the onshore backup add-on (how it would be priced / committed).

We'd like to have a working redline by the 12th so procurement can run PO/approval cycles before year-end.

Thanks,
Olivia Martin
Senior Counsel, Aurum HealthTech
olivia.martin@aurum.ai

Attachment: DPA_redlines_aurum_v2.docx (annotated redline)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Martin <olivia.martin@aurum.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2029-11-03T14:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: retention windows & residency carveouts

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. Appreciate the timeline — we'll prioritize. Quick summary of what we can offer and proposed compromise language so your legal team has something tangible to review:

1) Primary retention:
- Proposal: 45-day default retention for customer content (an operational default that balances cache/latency economics).
- If Aurum requires 30 days as a strict contractual floor, we can accept 30 days as the committed minimum in the DPA, with a note that transient caches (ephemeral KV) may be excluded.

2) Backups and snapshot retention:
- Proposal: 120-day backup retention (we can commit to a maximum 120 days).
- We will add explicit controls: restoration requires authorized request from Aurum org admins and logged approval.

3) Onshore backup (EU carveout):
- We can provide an EU-located backup copy as an add-on (Dedicated/Private option). This includes geo-locked snapshot storage and a contractual commitment to block cross-border replication on demand.
- Commercial note: add-on fee or uplift for reserved onshore snapshot storage; propose a 15% uplift to the Dedicated footprint or a fixed monthly fee (we can attach pricing).

4) Proof of deletion:
- We can provide a deletion manifest + signed certificate within 10 business days for primary data and within 30 business days for backup snapshot tombstones (due to asynchronous tombstone propagation).

5) Audit logs:
- Default 12 months. We can scope to 90 days for specific jurisdictions on request, subject to an admin configuration and an agreement on incident-forensics retention.

Next steps:
- I've attached a proposed counter-redline (DPA_counter_20291103.docx) with the language above.
- Neha (security) — can you confirm operational timelines for backup tombstone propagation and proof-of-deletion cert cadence?
- Ben (sales) — I'll need a price option for the EU onshore backup add-on and a short MAP (mutual action plan) we can share with Aurum procurement.

If Aurum agrees to the 45/120 compromise we can mark those sections as "agreed in principle" and move redlines for the rest of the DPA. If you insist on a strict 30/90 we can take that to a legal escalation and confirm the operational implications (ephemeral cache carveouts, backup snapshot TTL).

Link to counter-redline and MAP: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDPAredlines
DocuSign placeholders: https://www.docusign.net/rs/signer?d=0a1b2c3d4e5f

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Legal (Contracts), Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: DPA_counter_20291103.docx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2029-11-04T10:10:00-05:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: retention windows & residency carveouts

Rachel / Ben — quick ops/engineering confirmation and a few constraints to capture in the redline:

- Tombstone propagation: when a primary delete request is issued, primary storage and active replicas are removed within 24-48 hours; backup snapshots are tombstoned asynchronously and then subject to our snapshot lifecycle (we can guarantee tombstone removal from snapstore within 30 days of tombstone issuance for EU onshore snapshots when the onshore backup add-on is active).

- Backups: snapshots are immutable files; we can mark them as "candidate for purge" immediately after a delete request, but full removal from object storage depends on lifecycle window. For the EU add-on we can shorten that lifecycle to 30 days for snapshots (vs 120 days default).

- KV cache / ephemeral stores: caches are considered ephemeral and excluded from the contractual retention floor — we will explicitly call this out in the DPA to avoid mismatch with user-visible retention.

- Proof of deletion manifest: we will provide a machine-generated manifest (list of object ids + timestamp) and a signed ops statement. For backups we need a 30-business-day window to reconcile cross-region tombstones and provide a consolidated manifest.

- Audit logs: our standard security telemetry is retained 180 days for internal forensic purposes. We can provide a customer-scoped audit log export (90 days) for EU datasets if Aurum signs the add-on and accepts an operational SLA (export window up to 48 hours).

Operational ask: can Aurum provide an example erasure playbook (one page) showing a sample DSAR workflow? That will help us map backlog/pipeline and meet the contract timeline.

I've attached our internal ops-erasure-playbook.pdf for reference (contains the internal steps and expected SLAs). Note the difference in observable vs actual deletion timing — please review section 2.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: ops-erasure-playbook.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Martin <olivia.martin@aurum.ai>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2029-11-08T09:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: retention windows & residency carveouts — MAP and next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks for the call and the details. We can move forward on the following commercial / project commitments if Aurum accepts the operational compromises Rachel and Neha outlined:

- Contract commitments: Acceptable in-principle language is 30-day contractual floor OR 45-day default + explicit carveout language for ephemeral caches. Aurum to confirm which option legal wants in the DPA.

- Onshore backup (EU) add-on: We will offer: (a) geo-locked EU snapshot storage, (b) tombstone purge window shortened to 30 days for those snapshots, (c) an administrative control to trigger cross-border block. Pricing: either a 15% uplift on reserved capacity for Dedicated nodes or a fixed monthly fee of $6,500 for footprints under 5TB.

- Proof-of-deletion: Redwood will provide a deletion manifest and signed certificate within 10 business days for primary data and within 30 business days for backup snapshot removal when the onshore add-on is selected.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) 11/12 — Agree redline in principle (legal confirmation)
2) 11/15 — Ops confirms final wording for manifest and tombstone purge SLA
3) 11/20 — Commercials finalized (add-on pricing appended)
4) 11/22 — DocuSign execution and procurement kickoff

I've attached a short MAP workbook (MAP_Aurum_Redwood_2029.xlsx) with milestones and deliverables. If Aurum is good with the 45/120 compromise we can move faster; if you require strict 30/90 we'll need a quick legal call to agree operational exceptions.

Will you confirm which retention floor legal prefers and whether Aurum wants to include the onshore add-on in the initial contract? Once you confirm I'll prepare a redline with the agreed commercial appendix and send to your procurement team for PO routing.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
